title: Identification and molecular characterization of a metagenome-derived L-lysine decarboxylase gene from subtropical soil microorganisms
author: Jie Deng

steps_raw.instruction: Section 1: The extraction of metagenomic DNA from subtropical soil samples
The extraction of metagenomic DNA from soil sample refers to the lab protocol and the method described by Zhou and Bürgmann with modifications.
Weigh 5 g soil sample and add 13.6 ml DNA extraction buffer, mix and store in -80 °C for 30 min.
Melting in 65 °C water bath, go to step2 for twice.
Add 20% SDS until the final concentration of 1%. Add the proteinase K to the final concentration of 100 µg mL−1. Incubate at 65 °C for 2 h, every 15 min blending up and down.

Centrifuge at 5,000 rpm for 10 min at room temperature. Collect the supernatant. The soil pellets are extracted two more times by adding 4.5 ml of the extraction buffer, storing in -80 °C for 10 min and melting in water bath, adding 20% SDS and proteinase K to the final concentration of 1% and 100 µg mL−1, respectively, incubating at 65 °C for 10 min, and centrifuging as before.
Supernatants from the three cycles of extractions are combined and mixed with an equal volume of CIA solution (chloroform/isoamyl alcohol = 24:1, V/V).
Centrifuge at 5,000 rpm for 10 min at room temperature. Collect the aqueous phase.
Add 0.6 volume of isopropano and precipitate for 1 h at room temperature.
Centrifuge at 12,000 rpm for 20 min at room temperature. Collect the precipitate.
Add cold 70% ethanol to wash the precipitate twice. Vacuum concentration to ethanol volatilization completely. Dissolve the DNA pellet in TE buffer and store in -20°C.
DNA extraction buffer:
100 mM Tris HCl (pH 8.0); 100 mM EDTA; 100 mM NaH2PO4; 1.5 M NaCl; 1% CTAB.
Section 2: The extraction of plasmid DNA.

The plasmid DNA is extracted by alkaline lysis method. The specific methods see the “Molecular cloning a laboratory manual” in chapter 1 “Plasmid and their usefulness in molecular cloning” in protocol 1 “Preparation of plasmid DNA by alkaline lysis with SDS: Minipreparation”.
Using alkaline lysis solution I, alkaline lysis solution II, alkaline lysis solution III and phenol chloroform solution are used in extraction process.
Alkaline lysis solution I: 50 mM glucose, 25 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0), 10 mM EDTA (pH 8.0). Alkaline lysis solution II: 0.2 M NaOH, 1% SDS. Alkaline lysis solution III: 5 M KAc, acetic acid, pH 4.8.
Section 3: Bioinformatics analysis
Multiple sequence alignment was conducted with Align X in Vector NTI (InforMax, North Bethesda, MD, USA)
A phylogenetic tree was generated with Molecular Evolutionary Genetics Analysis (MEGA 6.0) using the neighbor-joining method (Tempe, AZ, USA).

Protein homology modeling structure was constructed with the GalaxyWEB server (http://galaxy.seoklab.org/). The protein model quality was precisely evaluated using MOLPROBITY server (http://molprobity.biochem.duke.edu/).
The protein model was used for docking with PLP and L-lysine in Autodock 4.2 (La Jolla, CA, USA) with default parameters. The protein structure model was displayed using PyMOL (New York, NY, USA).
Section 4: Using dansyl chloride solution to derivative the 1,5-pentanediamine.
Deriving 1,5-pentanediamine was based on the method described by Yoon with modifications
The 1,5-pentanediamine standard (0.1 mL) is mixed with 20 µL of 2 M sodium hydroxide and 30 µL of saturated sodium bicarbonate solution.
Add 200 µL of dansyl chloride solution (10 mg/mL) to the mixture, and then incubate at 60°C for 30 min.
Add 100 µL 25% ammonium hydroxide to remove the residual dansyl chloride.
Adjust the volume of mixture to 2 mL by using acetonitrile.
The sample is prepared after filtered through 0.2 µm-pore-size filters.
Section 5: Determination of L-lysine decarboxylase activity by spectrophotometry.

The LDC activity was determined using 2, 4, 6-trinitrobenzenesulfonic acid (TNBS) as described by Kanjee with modifications; this method was based on the differential solubility of L-lysine and 1,5-pentanediamine reaction products in toluene. The L-lysine and TNBS could form TNP-Lysine, which is soluble in water but insoluble in toluene. The 1,5-pentanediamine and TNBS could form TNP- pentanediamine, which is insoluble in water but soluble in toluene.
The reaction mixture was composed of 0.1 mM PLP, 2 mM L-lysine HCl, 3 µg recombinant protein, and 0.2 M Na2HPO4/0.1 M citric acid (pH 6.5).

The mixture was terminated by adding 250 µL of 1M K2CO3. 200 µL of 9.6 mM TNBS was then added and the mixture was incubated for 5 min at 40 °C. Each sample was thoroughly mixed with 1 mL of toluene at the top speed of Vortex mixer for 1 min. The toluene layers were separated by centrifuging for 15 min at 4,000 rpm. The absorbance was determined at 340 nm.
